# Education in Greece: Overview and Structure
Education in Greece is governed by a structured framework encompassing preschool, primary, secondary, vocational, and tertiary levels. Preschool education is compulsory and begins at age 4, comprising one year of pre-kindergarten and one year of kindergarten, with English introduced early as part of the core curriculum. Primary education ("Dimotiko") covers six academic years (ages 6–12), transitioning from descriptive evaluations to alphabetic and then numeric grading systems. Secondary education is divided into lower secondary ("Gymnasium," ages 12–15, compulsory) and upper secondary ("Lyceum," ages 15–18, non-compulsory), each with specialized and general schools, as well as evening and vocational options. All educational stages generally start in September and end in June.
Upper secondary graduates must pass nationally standardized Pan-Hellenic Examinations for entry into higher education institutions. Vocational education is robust, with pathways allowing direct entry into the workforce or progression to tertiary studies, and includes various specialized schools and apprenticeship schemes. Tertiary education is provided by public and, recently, accredited private higher education institutions, with access determined by standardized exams and national qualifications frameworks.

# Curriculum, Special Types, and Lifelong Learning
The Greek curriculum emphasizes Modern Greek Language and Literature, sciences, mathematics, and foreign languages, with English mandatory across all school years and options for French or German. Secondary schools offer specialized tracks within Lyceums and Vocational Lyceums, ranging from humanities to STEM and applied arts. Public and experimental schools, specialty music and art schools, and schools serving marginalized or special-needs populations enrich the system. Lifelong learning and non-formal education are supported through Open Courses, online platforms, adult secondary schools, and vocational training centers. The Hellenic Qualification Framework (HQF) links formal and non-formal qualifications to EU standards, ensuring comparability and mobility within Europe. Education is provided free of charge at most public institutions and is closely supervised by the Ministry of Education.
